 G-Shock’s Affordable “CasiOak” Successor Is Here, and It Looks a Lot Like Another Bucket-List Sports Watch
 G-Shock says the 2500 series takes after its original 1983 octagonal watch. Some excited fans are convinced about another horological icon.
 G-Shock 
 By Jack Seemer 
 Published 14 hours ago 
 ·
 Share 
 See more of our coverage in your search results 
 If you buy from a link, we may earn a commission. Learn more 
 Well, it’s official, even though it wasn’t much of a surprise.
 G-Shock finally pulls back the curtain on its new 2500 series of analog watches , following both an accidental leak and teaser on social media.
 Welcome to Power Moves : Diving deep into the product and brand moves that can change where a category is headed. Discover more here . 
 Comprising nine individual models that span both resin and metal constructions, the 2500 series arrives in November as easily the brand’s most anticipated launch of the year.
 Available in November, the new 2500 series is G-Shock’s most anticipated release since the “CasiOak.” G-Shock 
 For the last few weeks, leaked photos of the launch variants have drawn comparisons to the Patek Philippe Nautilus designed by Gérald Genta half a century ago.
 That’s because the 2500 has a cushion-like case with soft corners and pronounced shoulders, mimicking the “ears” of Genta’s iconic 1976 design.
 It’s also fully analog, a rarity when it comes to G-Shock.
 The watch features an analog display and cushion-like case with soft corners and shoulders reminiscent of the Patek Philippe Nautilus. G-Shock 
 Available in nine variants, two models have metal bracelets. G-Shock 
 Even the so-called “ CasiOak ,” which gets its nickname from another Genta design, the Audemars Piguet Royal Oak , displays the date via a small digital window.
 The 2500 series, meanwhile, pairs a three-cell date window at 3 o’clock with a small-seconds subdial at 9 o’clock.
 The face features a three-cell date window rather than a digital display. G-Shock 
 Shock factor
 At this point, connections to the Nautilus will be impossible for G-Shock to escape, especially considering the series’ unofficial nickname: “CasioNaut.”
 In fact, it should know after the “CasiOak” that such an association will only increase the excitement among the brand’s vast and loyal fandom.
 The 2500 series starts at $145 for the models made with bio-based resin. G-Shock 
 That said, G-Shock credits its own iconic timepiece as the true jumping-off point.
 According to the Japanese manufacturer, the 2500 was modeled after the DW-5000C from 1983, albeit as an analog-only display with “gentle curves catch light and shadow from every angle,” the brand says.
 Wearers can pause the seconds dial to extend the battery life up five years. G-Shock 
 Of course, the G-Shock name carries certain expectations. So just because the 2500 punches above its weight class in the looks department doesn’t mean it can’t take a tumble or two.
 For example, the minute hand is not directly fixed to the shaft but attaches magnetically to absorb and dissipate impact. All models also boast 200 meters of water resistance and a power-saving function that pauses the second hand to extend the battery life to five years.
 See below for the full roster.
 GMC-2500D-1A G-Shock 
 GMC-2500D-1A2 G-Shock 
 GMC-2500-1A8 G-Shock 
 GMC-2500G-9A G-Shock 
 GMC-2500-1A G-Shock 
 GAC-2500-1A G-Shock 
 GAC-2500-3A G-Shock 
 GAC-2500-9A G-Shock 
 GAC-2500-7A G-Shock 
 Availability and pricing
 Available in nine variants at launch, the 2500 series goes on sale in November with prices starting at $145 for the resin models (GAC2500-1A, -3A, -7A and -9A).
 The metal-accented GMC2500-1A, -1A8 and -9A cost between $280 and $300, while the GMC2500D-1A and -1A2, each equipped with a metal bracelet, cost $350.
